outlooks.summary: Scattered severe storms are most likely across parts of the Dakotas from mid-afternoon into tonight with large hail, damaging winds, and a couple tornadoes possible. A cluster of strong to isolated severe storms producing damaging winds may occur across parts of central/southern Illinois this afternoon to around sunset.

sections.title: Dakotas to northeast WY
sections.text: A broad mid-level trough will gradually shift east across the Northwest through tonight. An associated surface cold front will likewise move slowly east across the Dakotas and south across the High Plains/Black Hills. Ahead of the front, boundary-layer dewpoints in the 60s will be maintained beneath a warm elevated mixed layer, which will cap the boundary layer and delay thunderstorm initiation along the front until mid-afternoon. Storms are first expected to form with the zone of ascent along the front from northwest SD into western ND, aided by surface heating/mixing within the west edge of the warm sector. Additional storms will also develop in the post-frontal upslope regime off the Big Horns. Convection will subsequently spread northeast into central ND this evening, and develop eastward across western/central SD. The greatest potential for supercells will be with the convection that emanates across northeast WY and western SD, yielding a risk for a couple tornadoes and very large hail. Stronger mid-upper flow should tend to lag the front with predominately meridional wind profiles along the boundary, especially across western ND. As such, relatively rapid growth into multicel

sections.title: Midwest to Mid-Atlantic
sections.text: A series of MCVs will move east-southeastward along a stalled front from IA across IL/IN to the Chesapeake region through tonight. A combination of daytime heating and ascent focused by the most pronounced MCV over IL/IN, as well as related convective outflows, will aid in focusing a thunderstorm cluster across the OH Valley from IN/KY into OH/WV. Poor mid-level lapse rates should limit the overall risk, but isolated downburst winds are possible. A separate cluster should form this afternoon and persist into early evening from southeast IA across central IL in association with residual outflow boundaries and the upstream MCV now over western IA. This corridor will have comparatively larger MLCAPE as robust diabatic heating is underway across the Mid-MS Valley. The potential for a semi-organized cluster producing strong gusts and damaging winds is most likely within this region. A third somewhat clustered area of convection is expected this afternoon across VA/MD vicinity south of a lead impulse crossing the diffuse baroclinic zone near the MD/PA border. Mid-level lapse rates will be weak amid modest flow aloft. Isolated downburst winds should be the main hazard.

sections.title: Northwest TX
sections.text: Isolated to scattered high-based thunderstorm development is expected by late afternoon along the surface lee trough near the TX/NM border, aided by approach of a weak mid-level trough over central NM. With weak low/mid-level winds and modest upper-level flow, convection should struggle to organize. Isolated strong wind gusts are possible into the evening prior to stabilization of the boundary layer, but the risk for organized severe storms appears low. ..Grams/Gleason.. 06/10/2018

outlooks.summary: Scattered severe storms are most likely across parts of the Dakotas from this afternoon into tonight with large hail, damaging winds, and a couple tornadoes possible. A cluster of strong/severe storms producing damaging winds will spread across parts of central/southern Illinois into central Indiana into early evening.

sections.title: 20z Discussion
sections.text: 15% Severe probs have been expanded across the OH Valley. Early-day convection that developed across central IL has gradually evolved into an MCS. This activity is now growing upscale in areal coverage/intensity as it begins to surge southeast toward west-central IN. Precip shield is expanding across central IL and this appears partly responsible for a bulging squall line that is accelerating southeast in excess of 35kt. Have expanded 15% wind probs downstream to account for this maturing thunderstorm complex and the likelihood for this convection to spread farther than originally expected. Elsewhere, earlier thoughts regarding the evolution of convective initiation across the northern High Plains remain. ..Darrow.. 06/10/2018 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1130 AM CDT Sun Jun 10 2018/

outlooks.summary: Thunderstorms may continue to pose a risk for mainly severe hail and wind across the western into central Dakotas this evening, and perhaps the eastern Dakotas overnight.

sections.title: 01Z Outlook Update
sections.text: As large-scale mid/upper troughing continues shifting east/northeast of the Canadian and northern U.S. Rockies, the primary associated surface cyclone is now well north of the international border area, across the Canadian Prairies, and migrating northward. A trailing cold front has advanced east of the Rockies into the northern U.S. Plains, with strongest thunderstorm development generally focused immediately ahead of it, as far south as the Black Hills vicinity. With a plume of very warm elevated mixed layer air contributing to substantial inhibition ahead of the cold front, and stronger mid/upper flow and cold air aloft lagging to the west of the front, the extent of convective potential after the onset of boundary layer cooling by the 03-06Z time frame remains unclear. Across the eastern Dakotas into the upper Mississippi Valley, a cooler and drier low-level environment probably will suppress convective potential as the cold front advances eastward. In the near term though, a corridor of seasonably moist air continues to support moderate to large CAPE in the presence of steep lower/mid tropospheric lapses rates across the western into central Dakotas. mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated hail and damaging wind gusts are possible across portions of the lower and middle OH Valley during the next few hours. Isolated and marginal nature of the threat will likely preclude the need for a watch this morning into the early afternoon. However, late afternoon thunderstorms across western and central IL will likely merit an upgrade to Slight risk in the upcoming 1630Z Convective Outlook.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Cluster of thunderstorms currently moving through east-central IL and central IN, which originated via warm-air advection in the wake of an overnight MCS, will continue to move southeastward across the OH Valley. This cluster is displaced northward of the better instability, suggesting a relatively low threat for severe thunderstorms. Some hail may be possible as a result of storm interaction, particularly on the back building west end of the cluster, but the overall severe threat appears low. More cellular convection has recently developed across far southern IN and adjacent portions of western KY along the leading outflow from the overnight MCS. As with areas farther north, a generally isolated severe threat is expected given the lack of instability and displacement south of the stronger flow aloft. A few water-loaded downdrafts capable of damaging wind gusts constitute the highest severe hazard. Farther west, a complex surface pattern exists. A surface low was analyzed just north of the IA/MO/IL border intersection with an effective warm front extending southeastward across central IL. Warm air advection across this boundary is supporting backbuilding convection near PIA. As mentioned previously, some isolated hail is possible in this area. A more widespread severe threat may develop across western IL this afternoon along and south/southwest of the warm front and an upgrade to Slight risk is probable with the upcoming 1630Z Convective Outlook.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Damaging wind gusts and isolated hail are possible over the region this afternoon. Convective trends across the region will be monitored closely for increasing storm strength and a watch will likely be needed eventually.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Abundant cloudiness and precipitation is helping to maintain an effective warm front from southern IN northwestward to a weak surface low about 25 mi E of BRL in far west-central IL. Airmass south/southwest of this warm front is cloud-free, warm, and moist. Latest mesoanalysis estimates MLCAPE near 2000 J/kg with little remaining convective inhibition. Thunderstorms have developed upstream of this warm and destabilizing airmass across west-central IL, along an outflow boundary surging southeastward. Given the downstream instability, general expectation is for storms to continue developing along this outflow boundary. This area is on the southern fringe of the better flow aloft but enough overlap exists for some potential organization with the resulting MCS capable of damaging wind gusts. Even if solid organization doesn't occur, strong updrafts along the outflow could still result in water-loading and the potential for damaging wind gusts. Additionally, some isolated hail is possible, particularly as a result of storm mergers and brief updraft intensification.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for large hail, damaging winds, and a couple of tornadoes is increasing this afternoon. One or more watches will be issued by 4 PM CDT to address this threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: 19Z surface analysis and recent visible satellite imagery place a cold front across far western ND/northwestern SD, continuing into northeastern WY. 19Z RAP mesoanalysis shows convective inhibition decreasing across the western Dakotas as temperatures warm into the 80s with dewpoints remaining in the mid to upper 60s. Steep mid-level lapse rates emanating from the northern/central High Plains/Rockies have overspread this region, and resultant strong instability, with MLCAPE around 2000-3500 J/kg, has developed ahead of the front this afternoon. Large-scale lift associated with an upper trough over the northern Rockies and low-level convergence along the front will initiate thunderstorms, likely around 20-21Z. Initial development along the front should be discrete/supercellular given 35-50 kt of effective bulk shear. Scattered large hail and damaging winds are expected, with some potential for isolated very large hail greater than 2 inches in diameter across northwestern SD/southwestern ND where instability will be greatest. A couple of tornadoes may also occur across this region in the vicinity of a surface triple point where low-level winds should remain backed to southeasterly, and in part of northeastern WY within a post-frontal upslope flow regime. With the strongest mid-level winds forecast to slightly lag the surface front and given the linear low-level forcing, convection will very likely grow upscale this evening into one or more bowing line segments. Damaging winds should therefore become the primary severe threat with time as thunderstorms move eastward into the central Dakotas.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Occasional damaging wind gusts and isolated hail are possible as thunderstorm coverage increases over the next several hours. Isolated and marginal nature of the severe threat will preclude the need for a watch.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Thunderstorms have developed across the central Appalachians over the past 2 hours as a result of modest surface convergence and augmented lift along the higher terrain. Large-scale forcing for ascent is nebulous but the downstream airmass is warm, moist, and unstable, suggesting the probability of continued development/discrete propagation into much of VA and central NC. The airmass is weakly sheared with limited storm organization anticipated. Even so, moist airmass is supportive of wet downbursts within the strongest storms. Isolated hail is also possible, primarily as a result of storm mergers and consequential brief updraft intensification. Isolated and marginal nature of the severe threat will preclude the need for a watch.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat for damaging wind gusts and perhaps a tornado or two continues across east-central IL. Downstream threat across west-central IN will likely merit the issuance of another watch soon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MCS moving across central IL has recently exhibited an increase in forward motion, likely as a result of increased forward propagation into the warm, moist, and inhibition-free airmass downstream. New storm development as also occurred ahead of the line, increasing the probability for continued forward propagation. Current storm motion is estimated as 310 degrees at 35 kt. Northern portion of the line appears to be moving a little faster (i.e. closer to 40 kt). This southeastward progression will likely take the northern portion of the line to the edge of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 168 by 20Z. Downstream airmass across west-central/southern IN remains favorable for continued MCS progression and downstream watch will likely be needed soon. One other item of note is the increased southeasterly winds in place immediately along the warm front draped from near CMI southward into far southwest IN. Resulting localized enhancement of the low-level shear may contribute to brief tornado potential.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated storms have developed across parts of west-central IL near the western edge of WW 168. Should convective trends warrant, a westward expansion of WW 168 may be needed.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An outflow boundary is draped across the MCD area, left behind by early MCD/bow echo now tracking across east-central IL and IN. Storms have begun to develop in the vicinity of this boundary across parts of western IL from Adams County to SPI. Furthermore, a healthy CU field is present in visible satellite imagery across parts of northeast MO and west-central IL along axis of great instability and on the southern periphery of modest deep layer shear. Should convection intensify and become better organized along the outflow boundary and/or develop in the warm sector ahead of the boundary, WW 168 may need to be expanded westward to address this threat. Convective trends will be monitored. ..Leitman.. 06/10/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An isolated severe threat may persist across and just south of WW 169 the next couple of hours, but overall threat is diminishing. A downstream watch is not expected at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Bow echo tracking south/southeast into southern IN has been weakening over the last hour or so. The downstream airmass has been impacted by earlier day convection. As a result, instability wanes and inhibition increases with southward extent into northern KY. As such, gradual weakening should continue. A few stronger storms may persist on the southwestern periphery of the watch area along the axis of greater instability. But, these storms also will move toward the poorer quality airmass. Given overall trends and expected diminishing threat, a downstream watch is not anticipated at this time. ..Leitman.. 06/10/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe risk continues over western North Dakota across WW 170.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest visible satellite and radar loops show storms developing along the north-south cold front crossing western North Dakota at this time. Ahead of the front, an axis of moderate instability is in place, which should support continued storm development/growth. With storms likely to become linear with time, given linear forcing and largely meridional flow, a few stronger/damaging gusts along with hail will remain the primary severe risks across this region. ..Goss.. 06/10/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe risk -- including potential for a couple of tornadoes -- continues across WW 171.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Recent radar loop shows isolated storms developing near a cold front moving across northeast Wyoming and western South Dakota. The most vigorous storm remains the right-moving/cyclonic member of a recent storm split, that is moving across far southeast Harding County. This storm continues to exhibit broad rotation -- and has recently produced baseball-sized hail. With a moist/strongly unstable airmass (mixed-layer CAPE in excess of 4000 J/kg) ahead of the cold front and along and south of a warm front bisecting western South Dakota from northwest to southeast, additional storms will likely develop as ascent associated with the advancing upper system overspreads the area. Low-level southeasterly flow veering/increasing to southwesterly aloft will provide shear supportive of supercells, with a tornado or two possible in addition to very large hail and locally damaging gusts. With time, CAMs continue to suggest gradual upscale/linear growth, which would likely yield an increase in damaging wind risk. ..Goss.. 06/10/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat will slowly decrease with time. Convective trends will be monitored, but no re-issuance or extension of a WW is expected at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Linear, southward propagating segments of a mature MCS are currently moving across southern portions of Severe Thunderstorm Watches 0168 and 0169. While the atmosphere remains unstable, the onset of nocturnal cooling and subsequent stabilization of the boundary layer will result in storms becoming increasingly elevated with time. As the MCS continues to propagate southward away from the stronger mid-level flow, forward motion will be mainly driven by the strength of the cold pool, with storm outflow becoming increasingly likely to outrun convective updrafts. As such, the severe threat is expected to diminish with time and further watch issuance/extensions are not expected at this time.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe risk -- along with lingering/isolated tornado risk -- continues across Tornado Watch 171.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: As a cold front continues to advance across western South Dakota, storm mode continues to trend away from cellular toward a more linear configuration. As such, overall risk continues to gradually transition toward mainly damaging winds -- and possibly hail. Still, with a background kinematic environment supportive of supercells, some tornado risk will likely continue over the next couple of hours. In addition, a cluster/band of storms has developed just south of the current watch -- over Oglala Lakota County South Dakota and into northern Sheridan County, Nebraska. As such, a watch extension in area into the southern-most South Dakota counties may be considered. ..Goss.. 06/11/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Risk for damaging winds and marginally severe hail continues across WW 170.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A fairly well-organized line of storms continues moving east across western North Dakota, near an advancing north-south cold front. With the downstream thermodynamic environment sufficient to maintain convection, and shear supportive of organized storms, expect limited risk for locally damaging winds and/or hail to continue in the short term. ..Goss.. 06/11/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Limited severe risk may continue beyond the 04Z expiration of watches 170 and 171. Need for a downstream WW is being considered.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest radar loop shows a solid line of storms extending from southwest Manitoba into northern North Dakota, which has diminished in intensity over the past 1-2 hours. With this convection moving through the axis of greatest instability at this time, a boundary layer that continues to cool/stabilize, and with flow aloft largely line-parallel, prospects for appreciable downstream severe risk appear low. Farther south across South Dakota, a more unstable environment persists. In addition, storm mode remains more cellular -- in part due to a slightly more westerly flow component at mid levels. With greater -- though still gradually diminishing -- severe risk evident in this area, the need for a new severe thunderstorm watch remains in question but is being considered. ..Goss.. 06/11/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
